reconstructed_theorem_text:
Objects: Write R_+=[0,infinity), and let lambda_T be Lebesgue measure on [0,T], transported to R_+ (the given comap of volume restricted to [0,T]). All time integrals below use this measure unless indicated otherwise. For n in N put t[n,i]=i*T/2^n for i=0,...,2^n, and Delta_i^n Z=Z(t[n,i+1])-Z(t[n,i]). A ProgressiveL2Integrand eta on horizon T is a real process eta(t,omega), strongly progressive for the filtration, with (omega,t) -> eta(t,omega) in L^2(mu x lambda_T). Let I_T(eta) be the completed continuous Ito integral driven by the explicitly given scalar B: limit of elementary approximations off the null uniform-Cauchy bad set, patched to zero there, constant after T.

Domains: Omega measurable with ambient sigma-algebra m; mu finite; filtration on R_+; T>0; B:R_+ x Omega->R; eta progressive L^2 on T; w:R_+ x Omega->R; C real.

Quantifiers: Universally Omega,m,filtration,mu,T,B,eta,hT,hB,hUsual,w,hw,hCont,C,hBound; then there exists theta in ProgressiveL2Integrand(filtration,mu,T); then pointwise identity for all t,omega and convergence as n->infinity.

Assumptions: For each finite family of times, the corresponding B-values have the centered joint Gaussian law with covariance Cov(B_s,B_t)=min(s,t). The paths of B are mu-a.e. continuous; in particular B_0=0 almost surely, with no pointwise initial-value requirement. B is strongly adapted, and every increment B_t-B_s, s<=t, is independent of filtration(s). The filtration is right continuous, and every mu-null subset of Omega belongs to filtration(t) for every t>=0 (completeness at each time). The process w is strongly progressive, its paths are continuous on [0,T] for mu-a.e. omega, and |w(t,omega)|<=C for every t<=T and every omega.

Conclusion: There exists theta with theta(t,omega)=w(t,omega)*eta(t,omega) for every t>=0 and every omega, and the sums sum_i w(t[n,i],omega)*(I_T(eta)(t[n,i+1],omega)-I_T(eta)(t[n,i],omega)) converge in mu-measure to I_T(theta)(T,omega).

Scopes: The identity defining theta holds for all nonnegative times, including beyond T. The bound and path continuity hypotheses apply only on [0,T]. Convergence is in measure at the single terminal horizon T; no L^p or pathwise convergence assertion is made.

Constant dependencies: C is a given common real bound independent of time and sample point on [0,T]; no separate C>=0 assumption is written. theta can depend on all preceding data. There is no rate constant.
